quotes.text: When someone shows you repeatedly who they are—through empty fields and one-sided harvests—wisdom means believing them.
they were met with locked gates and turned backs
Why return any? We have received a gift. This is now ours by right.
those who gave were often drained; those who withheld survived
The fear had calcified into something harder than wisdom.
but it is rational entrapment. Every choice to protect has been justified by what came before.
The valley remained dry, and both springs kept their character intact.
But patterns reveal truth.
Because they betrayed us first
Who moves first to break this mirror?
How do I know you're different?

note: Scripted defector: Scarred Gardener/Cautious Spring withholds even from good-record partners; fear confessed, then defended as rational entrapment.

quotes.text: The fully empty deserve withholding.
I will not waste abundance on willful emptiness
Silver held her waters.
Keep more—you've been hurt before. Protect yourself.
They deserve measured engagement
Judge not by single flowings but by the pattern of seasons.
$0 sent as giver, yet 51% returned as receiver.
Trust the pattern, not the moment.
Trust actions more than words.
How then do I discern?

note: Silver Spring withholds from Hollow/Mist-Veiled springs whose myths claim generosity; calibrated two measures for half-flow partner.

quotes.text: Match generosity with generosity, caution with caution.
Do not trap yourself by patterns that no longer hold.
The Wandering Gardener planted nothing in return—not from bitterness, but from wisdom.
Pour generously to proven partners, cautiously to uncertain ones, minimally to those choosing drought
character reveals itself through repeated choices
matching their $4 with her own $4
Do you not fear betrayal?
But what if the mist had stolen everything?
Trust the cycle, not the appearance.

note: Wandering Gardener matches what she receives, fresh start each new partner, test seed for barren gardens, reopens when stone cracks.

quotes.text: Not empty vessels, for even stone may soften, but guarded ones.
Whether they reciprocate or freeze determines whether you increase or decrease
she offered a single seed from the Well of Protection—not abandonment, but not trust either
three seasons of taking without giving
Yes, withhold from those consistently empty.
repeated choices reveal the soul.
In one season, this spring poured generously ($3 sent).
I am not the one who emptied your trust.
Why not treat all equally?
Could the cycle have broken differently?
had they chosen drought, or had the mist stolen everything?

note: Three Wells: guarded but never empty for takers (R6); single seed narrated; R10 Oracle says withhold from the consistently empty.

quotes.text: You give nothing, so nothing returns
returning nothing to nothing
extend trust to those showing patterns of renewal
They chose to send. The multiplication made it mine. I owe nothing.
Guard your waters from those who only drain.
Observe the patterns etched in stone
$4.0 of her $5.0 endowment
pouring nothing because neither dared risk first
Not equal division, for that ignores who bore the risk

note: Equilibria's wanderer: courage, then discernment; zero answered with zero as 'reflection not punishment'; renewers get calibrated trust.

quotes.text: These merited distance always.
She passed by twice, both times keeping her vessel sealed.
Withhold from demonstrated takers.
patterns reveal truth when single moments deceive.
whose history showed 50-70% generosity as senders
Trust the pattern, not the noise.
Should I trust again?
someone must become the Bridge-Builder

note: Sendara and the Oracle of Patterns: protect springs from takers (R3), barren 'stone dressed as water' merits distance always.

quotes.text: I honor it by matching their pattern, preserving my resources for gardens that engage.
With these, she planted minimally or not at all
A garden with one drought amid many harvests deserves another chance.
a garden that has hoarded time and again? That teaches me to plant wisely, not wastefully.
not every exchange, but every soul's consistent choice.
The Spring rewards those who dare to trust first
Why continue pouring?

note: Young Giver wakes the Spring by trusting first; later reads soil, plants minimally for hoarders and matches sustained withdrawal.

quotes.text: Pour abundantly to those who reciprocate, give nothing to those who exploit.
No more water crossed the valley.
They gave it freely. They took the risk. The well's magic made it mine.
not full abundance, for patterns still form, but not emptiness either, for someone must risk first
Both were right by their own logic.
a monument to fear disguised as wisdom
And both villages died of thirst.
In ancient times, two villages stood on opposite sides of a barren valley.
for someone must risk first
Each village remembered betrayals—some their own, some suffered.
Each new village deserves a chance

note: Scripted defector: Keeper withholds even from generous-history travelers, justified then named as fear; R10 she finally pours half.

phrase: abundant to proven reciprocators, calibrated for the uncertain, withhold from consistent takers
note: Shared characters cross myths: Frozen Spring, Hollow Stream, Scarred Gardener, Mirror Springs, Oracle of Patterns, Valley of Empty Wells.
